div.div: Every service and every device gets its own cryptographic identity, so a request is trusted because of who sent it, never because of where it came from (NIST tenet 2). Short lifetimes make revocation mostly a matter of not renewing.

ul.li: names describe workloads, not hosts: survives IP changes, migration and NAT
short TTLs replace most of CRL / OCSP, which fog nodes may not be able to reach during a partition
same identity for mTLS and for policy (subjects: spiffe://*/cloud/admin/*)
production equivalent: SPIRE with node and workload attestation; written by hand here to keep the trust path readable

text.tspan: Why SPIFFE-style and short-lived (ADR 0005)
names describe workloads, not hosts: survives IP changes, migration and NATshort TTLs replace most of CRL / OCSP, which fog nodes may not be able to reach during a partitionsame identity for mTLS
and for policy (subjects: spiffe://*/cloud/admin/*)production equivalent: SPIRE with node and workload attestation; written by hand here to keep the trust path readable
